objective: Learners compute the full cost of an invented insurance arrangement including premiums and deductible, and compare it against bearing a loss unprotected.
scenario: Nils is a made-up seventh grader modelling a pretend policy: $45.00 a month in invented premiums, a $500.00 deductible, and a covered invented $3,200.00 repair. All figures are invented and describe no real policy.
safetyNotes: Every amount, person, business, and account in this task is invented for practice. Nothing here refers to a real household.
Never write a real bank account, card, PIN, password, Social Security, or tax number on this sheet; the task never asks for one.
This is education, not individualized financial advice. Real money decisions belong to a trusted adult.
This policy is invented for the exercise and is not a recommendation about any real insurance product.

tasks.directions: Compute a simulated year of Nils's invented premiums at $45.00 a month.

prompts.text: What do 12 months of premiums cost?

tasks.directions: Add the deductible Nils pays on the claim to the year of premiums to reach his total cost in the year of the repair.

prompts.text: What is the total cost in the claim year with the policy?
How much better off is Nils with the policy in that year?

tasks.directions: Model three quiet simulated years with no claim at all, then compare against the single claim year.

prompts.text: What do three quiet years of premiums cost?
Across those three quiet years plus the claim year, how much better off is Nils than paying the repair unprotected?

tasks.directions: Four years of premiums nearly matched the repair.

prompts.text: Explain what Nils is actually buying with the premiums, and describe the situation in which the policy is worth having even if the arithmetic comes out roughly even.

remediation: If a learner omits the deductible, list Nils's premiums and deductible as separate labelled lines before any total is computed.
extension: Ask the learner how many quiet years Nils could pay for before the policy costs more than the repair, and to show the reasoning.
